summary: Commodity Channel Index: how far typical price sits from its 20-bar average, in units of mean deviation, with plus and minus 100 levels.
overview: The Commodity Channel Index (CCI) shows how far price has moved from its average, in its own pane. Reference levels sit at +100 and -100.
The line and fill are green above zero and red below.
how: CCI = (source - SMA(source, 20)) / (0.015 x mean absolute deviation). The source is typical price, (high + low + close) / 3, by default.
The 0.015 constant scales the result so most readings fall between -100 and +100.
use: Some traders read moves above +100 as strong upside and below -100 as strong downside.
Use returns inside the levels to see a move losing pace.
Watch zero-line crosses for changes in direction.
Look for divergence between CCI and price.
alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
CCI has no fixed upper or lower limit.
